title: refactor(plugin-dashboard): one auto-refresh timer for both dashboard surfaces, pinned by call counts (objectui#8820)
body:
Fixes #8820
Clause-②: no

## What changed

`DashboardGridLayout` and `DashboardRenderer` each carried their own copy of the dashboard auto-refresh logic: a `refreshing` flag, a `handleRefresh` callback used by both the "Refresh All" button and the timer, and an effect that read `refreshIntervalSeconds` and drove `setInterval`. Both surfaces now call one hook, `useDashboardAutoRefresh` (new file `packages/plugin-dashboard/src/useDashboardAutoRefresh.ts`), which is that logic moved unchanged. The authored period is now read in one place. The hook is internal: the package entry is not touched.

A new pin, `packages/plugin-dashboard/src/__tests__/dashboardAutoRefreshTimer.test.tsx`, mounts both components and counts `onRefresh` calls under fake timers.

## Base re-read, measured on `42687baf2` before any edit

- The two timers were identical in logic: the same `refreshing` state, the same `handleRefresh` body (`setRefreshing(true)`, `onRefresh()`, a 600ms reset), the same early return (no timer when `refreshIntervalSeconds` is falsy, is zero or less, or `onRefresh` is missing), the same `setInterval(handleRefresh, schema.refreshIntervalSeconds * 1000)`, and the same dependency list `[schema.refreshIntervalSeconds, onRefresh, handleRefresh]`. They differed only in comments and in `React.useX` versus named imports.
- Each read only `refreshIntervalSeconds`. The string `refreshInterval` appears in both files only inside comments.
- The installed `@objectstack/spec` is 17.4.0, and its `DashboardSchema` refuses `refreshInterval` by name (`safeParse` answers `invalid_type` on that path, with the rename message). So the hook reads one key and has no fallback.

## Why this is behaviour-neutral

- The gate, the seconds-to-milliseconds arithmetic and the dependency list are copied as they were.
- The effect keeps the interval id in an effect-local constant instead of `intervalRef`. The ref was read only by the cleanup of the effect that wrote it, so the two forms clear the same interval in every sequence.
- In `DashboardRenderer` the hook call sits where the old `handleRefresh` and effect sat, so the refresh effect keeps its order relative to the component's other effects. In `DashboardGridLayout` it sits where that component's effect sat.

## Departures from the prior-art branch (`claude/issue-8820-dashboard-refresh-interval-seconds`, `e5d95e1a4`)

That branch was not pushed to or rewritten; this is a new branch.

- **Dropped the both-spelling read**, as the card asks.
- **Dropped the number-only filter** (`resolveRefreshIntervalSeconds`, which refused a string `'30'` and `NaN`). On base, the early return only rejects a falsy or non-positive value, so it starts a 30s timer for a string `'30'`, and refusing it would be a behaviour change beyond de-duplication.
- **Did not carry** its edits to the published `inputs` row, the config panel, or the i18n overlay: the card puts them out of scope, and objectui#8783 has already moved them.
- **Reworked the pin** for a single spelling. The missing-handler case now counts pending timers instead of only asserting that nothing throws. New cases: a changed period re-arming (the card names it), a negative period, the retired spelling, the phase across an equal-period re-render, a handler swap, and the de-duplication case.

## The pin: 11 cases per surface, 22 in all

Each block is `describe.each` over both components, so a failure names the surface.

1. fires every `refreshIntervalSeconds` seconds (30s period, 95s elapsed: exactly 3 calls, none before the first period);
2. does not start when no period is authored;
3. and 4. does not start for a period of `0` or `-30`;
5. does not read the retired `refreshInterval` spelling;
6. arms no interval without an `onRefresh` host handler (pending fake-timer count, with a control leg: the same period plus a handler arms exactly one more timer than no period);
7. stops when the dashboard unmounts;
8. re-arms on a changed period: 30s becomes 60s at t=30s, there is no second call by t=89s, and there is one at t=90s;
9. keeps its phase across a re-render that repeats the same period in a new schema object;
10. calls the current `onRefresh` after the host swaps it, never the old one;
11. takes its timer from the shared `useDashboardAutoRefresh` hook (the de-duplication case: the real hook is wrapped in a `vi.fn` passthrough).

## Evidence

All test and type-check runs went through `os-verify-lock`. Each verdict below is the one the tool printed. The base leg and the ablation ran at `b98eb6164`. The last commit, `f990a9997`, changes only comments in the hook and the pin plus one changeset sentence, and everything else below was rerun on it.

- **Base leg** (the two components checked out at `42687baf2`, with the new hook and pin present). Predicted before the run: only case 11 goes red, on both surfaces. Observed: `Tests 2 failed | 20 passed (22)`. The two failures are the case-11 pair, each reading `Number of calls: 0`. The firing cases are green on base because base's two copies do fire; firing is proven load-bearing by the ablation below. Restore was `git checkout HEAD --` on absolute paths inside a trap. After it, the two blobs were back to their HEAD hashes (`6b2cf9e46`, `bde5d0e96`), `git diff HEAD` was empty and `git status --porcelain` was empty.
- **Reader ablation**, through `ablation-replace.mjs`. The anchor `const seconds = schema.refreshIntervalSeconds;` became `const seconds = undefined as number | undefined;`. On disk: anchor x1 to x0, replacement x0 to x1, blob `dd029bbd0484` to `5e8e6e2ffff3`. Predicted before the run: cases 1 and 6 to 10 go red on both surfaces (12), and cases 2 to 5 and 11 stay green (10). Case 6 goes red through its control leg. Observed: `Tests 12 failed | 10 passed (22)`, exactly that set. Restore: `blob == HEAD (dd029bbd0484) and git diff HEAD is empty`, and the tree was clean afterwards. No `dist/` is involved: the pin imports the components and the hook by relative `src` paths.
- **`@object-ui/plugin-dashboard` suite plus the derived suites below, in one run** at `f990a9997`: `Test Files 171 passed (171)`, `Tests 2123 passed | 6 skipped (2129)`. At `b98eb6164` the same two sets, run separately, gave 150 files (1368 passed, 6 skipped) and 21 files (755 passed).
- **Type-check**: at `b98eb6164`, `turbo run type-check --filter=@object-ui/plugin-dashboard` built the dependencies first and gave `Tasks: 14 successful, 14 total`. At `f990a9997`, `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-dashboard type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) exited 0. `tsc --listFilesOnly` shows both `tsconfig.json` and `tsconfig.test.json` include the touched files.
- **Suites that read the touched files from disk or scan their corpus.** The set is: the `scripts/__tests__` suites for `vi-mock-specifiers`, `vi-mock-inherit`, `vi-mock-override-shape`, `markdown-test-inputs`, `one-authority-per-exported-name-6273`, `new-cross-file-line-citations`, `handler-key-read-sites`, `control-bytes`, `test-path-roots`, `unreferenced-sources`, `type-check-coverage`, `side-effects-declaration-consistency`, the six changeset suites and `changeset-polarity-census`; plus `packages/sdui-parser/src/__tests__/dashboard-widget-options-census.test.ts` and `examples/schema-catalog/test/plugin-dashboard-gallery-render.test.tsx`, which read or render these two components.
- **Pin at `f990a9997`**: all 22 cases pass inside the run above.
- **Gates** at `f990a9997`, each exit 0 with an OK verdict: `check-control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations` (`0 new citation(s)`), `check-vi-mock-specifiers`, `check-vi-mock-inherit`, `check-vi-mock-override-shape`, `check-test-path-roots`, `check-unreferenced-sources`, `check-type-check-coverage`, `check:self-import`, `check-phantom-dependencies`, `check:handler-key-reads`, `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `check-changeset-claims`, `check-changeset-overwrite`, `check-pending-changeset-literals`, and `check-governed-queue-guard --test` (`NOT GOVERNED`).
- **eslint, narrowed**, at `f990a9997`, to the four touched TypeScript files with `--no-inline-config`. The population is those four files; `eslint --print-config` resolves a config for each. The count comes from `--format json`: 4 files, 0 errors, 16 warnings. The same two components at `42687baf2` give 8 + 8 warnings with the same rule counts, and the two new files give none. `eslint.config.js` declares no `projectService` or `parserOptions.project`, so linting is not type-aware and this diff cannot move the verdict of any untouched file. The repo-wide `eslint .` run belongs to CI.

## Acceptance notes

- ⚠️ The hook's effect still lists `handleRefresh`, a `useCallback` identity, as a dependency. AGENTS.md commandment 10 bans this shape. It is carried over because this card changes no behaviour, and a comment in the hook says so. A fix is now one edit instead of two, and cases 9 and 10 pin the timing that such a fix has to keep. Not filed: it only shows under a forced memo discard, which this tree does not produce on its own.
- NOT MEASURED: `check:readme-exports`, because it needs every package's `dist/` on disk (`type entry ... is not on disk -- run pnpm build first`). This diff touches no README and no package export.
- NOT MEASURED locally: the full `pnpm test` and repo-wide lint. Both belong to CI.
